trials.name: GI-102 (CD80-IgG4 Fc-IL2v3) in Combination With Pasritamig in Patients With Metastatic Castration-resistant Prostate Cancer (mCRPC) (JET-201)
trials.officialTitle: A Phase 1b/2, Open-label, Multi-center Study to Evaluate the Anti-cancer Activity, Safety and Tolerability of GI-102 (CD80-IgG4 Fc-IL2v3) in Combination With Pasritamig [T-CELL-Redirecting Agent Targeting Human Kallikrein 2 (KLK2)] in Patients With Metastatic Castration-resistant Prostate Cancer (mCRPC) Who Progressed on Previous Novel Hormonal Therapy (NHT) (JET-201)
trials.assignment: registry drug/condition context; ownership and active pipeline not inferred

design.interventionModelDescription: Participants are assigned to receive GI-102 in combination with pasritamig sequentially across different dose levels during the Safety run-in phase based on safety and dose-escalation decisions. Participants may subsequently be enrolled in the Expansion phase at the combination recommended Phase 2 dose.

eligibility.eligibilityCriteria:
Key Inclusion Criteria:

* Male participants aged ≥18 years (or ≥19 years according to local regulatory requirements).
* ECOG performance status of 0 to 1.
* Histologically confirmed advanced prostate adenocarcinoma with measurable or evaluable disease. Adenocarcinoma with small cell or neuroendocrine (NE) features is permitted. However, primary small cell carcinoma, carcinoid tumor, mixed NE carcinoma, or large cell NE carcinoma (or pathologic evidence of conversion to) is disallowed.
* Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) with documented disease progression following at least one line of novel androgen receptor-targeted therapy.
* PSA ≥2 ng/mL at screening.
* No more than 2 prior taxane regimens and no prior cytotoxic chemotherapy other than taxane therapy.
* Prior orchiectomy or ongoing androgen deprivation therapy with castrate testosterone levels.
* Adequate organ and marrow function and adequate cardiovascular function.
* Adequate recovery from prior anticancer therapy-related adverse events.
* Willingness and ability to comply with study procedures and protocol-specified contraception requirements.

Key Exclusion Criteria:

* Active or prior CNS metastases, carcinomatous meningitis, or clinically unstable spinal cord compression.
* Significant uncontrolled cardiovascular, pulmonary, hepatic, autoimmune, infectious, or other systemic disease.
* Active or recent clinically significant infection, including active tuberculosis, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C.
* Active pneumonitis or interstitial lung disease (ILD), or history of clinically significant pneumonitis/ILD.
* Recent treatment with investigational products, prohibited immunomodulating agents, radiotherapy, major surgery, or other protocol-defined prohibited therapies.
* Prior treatment with CD3-directed therapies, including KLK2-CD3 bispecific antibodies or other CD3-targeting T-cell engagers.
* Known hypersensitivity to GI-102, pasritamig, or their excipients, or any other condition that may interfere with study participation or interpretation of results.

arms.label: Safety run-in: GI-102 + pasritamig (Schedule A)
arms.description: Participants receive GI-102 in combination with pasritamig during the Safety run-in phase. Dose escalation is guided by a Bayesian Optimal Interval (BOIN) design.

arms.label: Safety run-in: GI-102 + pasritamig (Schedule B)
arms.description: Participants receive GI-102 in combination with pasritamig during the Safety run-in phase. Dose escalation is guided by a Bayesian Optimal Interval (BOIN) design.

arms.label: Expansion
arms.description: Participants enrolled in the Expansion phase will receive the combination recommended Phase 2 regimen (cRP2R) of GI-102 and pasritamig, determined based on the safety and dose-escalation results from the Safety run-in phase.

interventions.name: GI-102
interventions.description: GI-102 will be administered in accordance with the procedures specified in the study protocol.

interventions.name: Pasritamig

primaryOutcomes.measure: Incidence and nature of DLTs (Safety run-in phase)
primaryOutcomes.description: A DLT is defined as a clinically significant AE (classified according to the NCI CTCAE version 6.0) or significant laboratory abnormality that occur during the DLT assessment periods, and is considered by the Investigator to be related to the study drug(s).
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: From Day -14 to Cycle 1 Day 22 (35 days)

primaryOutcomes.measure: Incidence, nature, and severity of AEs graded according to CTCAE v6.0 (Safety run-in phase)
primaryOutcomes.description: An adverse event (AE) is any untoward medical occurrence in a participant administered a pharmaceutical product and which does not necessarily have to have a causal relationship with the treatment. An AE can therefore be any unfavorable and unintended sign (including an abnormal laboratory finding, for example), symptom, or disease temporally associated with the use of a pharmaceutical product, whether or not considered related to the pharmaceutical product. Preexisting conditions which worsen during a study are also considered as AEs. All AE events will be graded according to National Cancer Institute (NCI) Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 6.0.

primaryOutcomes.measure: PSA response rate (≥ 50% decline from baseline) per PCWG3 (Expansion phase)
primaryOutcomes.description: PSA response rate is defined as the percentage of participants with a decline of PSA of 50% or more from baseline.

secondaryOutcomes.measure: PSA response rate (≥ 50% and ≥ 90% decline from baseline) per PCWG3 (Safety run-in phase)
secondaryOutcomes.description: PSA response rate is defined as the percentage of participants with a decline of PSA of 50% (or 90%) or more from baseline.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Up to 2 years

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Radiographic PFS per PCWG3
secondaryOutcomes.description: Radiographic PFS is defined as the time from the date of first dose of any study treatment until the date of radiographic disease progression or death, whichever comes first.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Up to 2 years

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Time to PSA progression
secondaryOutcomes.description: Time to PSA progression, defined as the time from baseline to the first date of documented PSA progression per PCWG3 criteria.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Up to 2 years

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Overall Response Rate (ORR) per RECIST v1.1
secondaryOutcomes.description: Among participants with measurable disease, ORR is defined as the percentage of participants who achieve a partial response (PR) or complete response (CR) according to RECIST v1.1.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Up to 2 years

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Duration of Response (DoR) per RECIST v1.1
secondaryOutcomes.description: Among participants with measurable disease who achieve a CR or PR, DoR is defined as the time from the first documented CR or PR until the first documented disease progression according to RECIST v1.1 or death from any cause, whichever occurs first.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Up to 2 years

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Disease Control Rate (DCR) per RECIST v1.1
secondaryOutcomes.description: Among participants with measurable disease, DCR is defined as the percentage of participants who achieve a CR, PR, or stable disease (SD) according to RECIST v1.1.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Up to 2 years

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Incidence, nature, and severity of AEs graded according to CTCAE v6.0 (Expansion phase)
secondaryOutcomes.description: An adverse event (AE) is any untoward medical occurrence in a participant administered a pharmaceutical product and which does not necessarily have to have a causal relationship with the treatment. An AE can therefore be any unfavorable and unintended sign (including an abnormal laboratory finding, for example), symptom, or disease temporally associated with the use of a pharmaceutical product, whether or not considered related to the pharmaceutical product. Preexisting conditions which worsen during a study are also considered as AEs. All AE events will be graded according to National Cancer Institute (NCI) Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 6.0.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Up to 2 years

secondaryOutcomes.measure: PK profile: peak plasma concentration (Cmax) of GI-102 when combined with pasritamig
secondaryOutcomes.description: Plasma concentrations of GI-102 will be measured at specified time points following administration of GI-102 in combination with pasritamig to determine the maximum observed plasma concentration (Cmax).
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Up to 2 years

secondaryOutcomes.measure: PK profile: half-life (T1/2) of GI-102 when combined with pasritamig
secondaryOutcomes.description: Plasma concentrations of GI-102 will be measured at specified time points following administration of GI-102 in combination with pasritamig to determine the terminal half-life (T1/2) of GI-102.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Up to 2 years

secondaryOutcomes.measure: PK profile: area under the plasma concentration-time curve (AUC) of GI-102 when combined with pasritamig

trials.name: GI-101/GI-101A as a Single Agent or in Combination With Pembrolizumab or Lenvatinib in Advanced Solid Tumors
trials.officialTitle: A Phase 1/2, Open-label, Dose-escalation, Dose-optimization and Expansion Study to Evaluate Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, and Therapeutic Activity of GI-101/GI-101A as a Single Agent and in Combination With Pembrolizumab or Lenvatinib in Patients With Advanced or Metastatic Solid Tumors (Keynote B59)
trials.assignment: registry drug/condition context; ownership and active pipeline not inferred

eligibility.eligibilityCriteria:
Key Inclusion Criteria:

* Males and females aged ≥ 18 years (or ≥ 19 years according to local regulatory guidelines) at the time of screening.
* Has adequate organ and marrow function as defined in protocol.
* Measurable disease as per RECIST v1.1.
* ECOG performance status 0-1.
* Adverse events related to any prior chemotherapy, radiotherapy, immunotherapy, other prior systemic anti-cancer therapy, or surgery must have resolved to Grade ≤1, except alopecia and Grade 2 peripheral neuropathy.
* HIV infected patients must be on anti-retroviral therapy (ART) and have a well-controlled HIV infection/disease as defined in protocol.

Key Exclusion Criteria:

* Has known active CNS metastases and/or carcinomatous meningitis.
* An active second malignancy
* Has active or a known history of Hepatitis B or known active Hepatitis C virus infection.
* Has active tuberculosis or has a known history of active tuberculosis
* Active or uncontrolled infections, or severe infection within 4 weeks before study treatment administration.
* History of chronic liver disease or evidence of hepatic cirrhosis, except patients with liver metastasis.
* Has an active autoimmune disease that has required systemic treatment in past 2 years.
* Previous immunotherapies related to mode of action of GI-101.
* Has a diagnosis of immunodeficiency or is receiving chronic systemic steroid therapy or any other form of immunosuppressive medications within 2 weeks prior to Cycle 1 Day 1.
* Administration of prior systemic anti-cancer therapy including investigational agents within 4 weeks prior to treatment.
* Radiotherapy within the last 2 weeks before start of study treatment administration, with exception of limited field palliative radiotherapy
* Administration of a live, attenuated vaccine within 4 weeks before Cycle 1 Day 1.
* Known hypersensitivity to any of the components of the drug products and/or excipients of GI-101/GI-101A, pembrolizumab or lenvatinib.

Other protocol defined inclusion exclusion criteria may apply. Cancer type and part-specific inclusion criteria are described in the study protocol.

trials.name: A Study to Evaluate the Effects of the Combination of GI-102 With GIB-7 on Biomarkers of Aging in Healthy Adults and Cancer Survivors
trials.officialTitle: Phase 2a, Proof-Of-Concept, Multi-National, 8-Week, Randomized, Single-Blinded, Placebo-Controlled Trial of GI-102 in Combination With GIB-7 to Evaluate Its Effects on Biomarkers of Aging in Healthy Adults and Cancer Survivors

eligibility.eligibilityCriteria:
Key Inclusion Criteria:

1. Must be aged between ≥18 and ≤80 years old at the time of informed consent.
2. At the discretion of the Investigator, must be in a state of general health that is not severely compromised (ie, no life-threatening illness or disability).
3. Participants with a history of cancer may be included only if they meet one of the following:

   1. Participants have been disease-free for ≥2 years; OR
   2. For those diagnosed within 2 years:

      * The cancer was treated with curative intent (eg, surgery, anti-cancer agents including chemotherapy)
      * Participants have been in remission for ≥12 months
      * Participants are not on any active cancer treatment except maintenance therapies (eg, endocrine therapy or bisphosphonates)
      * Participants must have received systemic anti-cancer therapies without immunotherapy for their cancers
4. Women of childbearing potential (WOCBP; see definition in Section 5.3) must agree to use a highly effective method of contraception from 14 days prior to Visit 2 until 180 days after the last dose of study medication (GI-102 or GIB-7). Fertile men must agree to use an acceptable method of contraception from 14 days prior to Visit 2 until 90 days after the last dose of study medication (GI-102 or GIB-7).

Key Exclusion Criteria:

1. Severe and poorly managed chronic diseases, such as advanced cardiovascular disease, kidney failure requiring transplant or dialysis, uncontrolled diabetes, detectable malignancy (≤ 2 years), severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), or untreatable, terminal cancer as judged by the Investigator or history of life threatening infection (eg, meningitis).
2. Dependent on walkers or wheelchairs; severe difficulty or inability to perform activities of daily living independently or inability to perform study measures required to test muscle function (an amputee is eligible if participants can walk without walkers or wheelchair) as judged by the Investigator.
3. Major surgery within the past 6 months or scheduled during the study period, including severe orthopedic diseases requiring joint replacement surgery.
4. History of substance abuse or dependency or history of recreational IV drug use over the last 5 years (by self-declaration).
5. Female participants who are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding during the study period. Participants undergoing perimenopause or the menopause transition are eligible.

trials.officialTitle: An Open-label, Multicenter, Dose Escalation and Expansion Phase 1/2 Study to Evaluate the Safety, Tolerability and Pharmacokinetics, and Anti-tumor Activity of GI-102, a CD80-IgG4 Fc-IL-2v Bispecific Fusion Protein, As a Single Agent and in Combination with Conventional Anti-cancer Drugs, Pembrolizumab or Trastuzumab Deruxtecan(T-DXd) in Patients with Advanced or Metastatic Solid Tumors (KEYNOTE-G08)
trials.assignment: registry drug/condition context; ownership and active pipeline not inferred

eligibility.eligibilityCriteria:
Key Inclusion Criteria:

* Males and females aged ≥ 18 years (or ≥ 19 years according to local regulatory guidelines) at the time of screening.
* Has adequate organ and marrow function as defined in protocol.
* Measurable disease as per RECIST v1.1.
* ECOG performance status 0-1.
* Adverse events related to any prior chemotherapy, radiotherapy, immunotherapy, other prior systemic anti-cancer therapy, or surgery must have resolved to Grade ≤1, except alopecia and Grade 2 peripheral neuropathy.
* HIV infected patients must be on anti-retroviral therapy (ART) and have a well-controlled HIV infection/disease as defined in protocol.

Key Exclusion Criteria:

* Has known active CNS metastases and/or carcinomatous meningitis.
* An active second malignancy.
* Has active or a known history of Hepatitis B or known active Hepatitis C virus infection.
* Has active tuberculosis or has a known history of active tuberculosis.
* Active or uncontrolled infections, or severe infection within 4 weeks before study treatment administration.
* History of chronic liver disease or evidence of hepatic cirrhosis, except patients with liver metastasis.
* Has an active autoimmune disease that has required systemic treatment in past 2 years.
* Previous immunotherapies related to mode of action of GI-102.
* Has a diagnosis of immunodeficiency or is receiving chronic systemic steroid therapy or any other form of immunosuppressive medications within 2 weeks prior to Cycle 1 Day 1.
* Administration of prior systemic anti-cancer therapy including investigational agents within 4 weeks prior to treatment.
* Radiotherapy within the last 2 weeks before start of study treatment administration, with exception of limited field palliative radiotherapy.
* Administration of a live, attenuated vaccine within 4 weeks before Cycle 1 Day 1.
* Known hypersensitivity to any of the components of the drug products and/or excipients of GI-102.

Other protocol defined inclusion exclusion criteria may apply

interventions.name: GI-102
interventions.description: Dose level will be escalated from 0.06 mg/kg to 0.45 mg/kg and Recommended phase 2 dose (or RP2D-1, RP2D+1) of GI-102 will be administered via IV infusion Q3W up to 2 years (approximately 35 years).

interventions.name: doxorubicin
interventions.description: Doxorubicin will be administered intravenously at a dose of 75 mg/m2 on Day 3 every 3-week (21-day) cycle for up to 6 cycles.

interventions.name: paclitaxel
interventions.description: Paclitaxel will be administered intravenously over 1 hour at a dose of 80 mg/m2 each time weekly as a diluted solution according to the prescribing information.

interventions.name: bevacizumab
interventions.description: Bevacizumab will be administered intravenously at a dose of 10 mg/kg every 2 weeks.

interventions.name: eribulin
interventions.description: Eribulin will be administered intravenously at a dose of over 1.4 mg/m2 over 2 to 5 minutes on Days 3 and 10 every 3-week (21-day) cycle.

interventions.name: trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd)
interventions.description: T-DXd will be administered initially as a 5.4 mg/kg (or 6.4 mg/kg only for gastric cancer) IV over 30 - 90 minutes every 3 weeks.

interventions.name: pembrolizumab
interventions.description: pembrolizumab will be administered at a dose of 200 mg as IV infusion Q3W.

interventions.name: GI-102
interventions.description: Recommended phase 2 dose (or RP2D-1, RP2D-2) of GI-102 will be administered via IV infusion Q3W up to 2 years (approximately 35 years).

primaryOutcomes.measure: Incidence and nature of Dose-Limiting Toxicity (DLTs) (dose escalation phase of Part A and B)
primaryOutcomes.description: A DLT is defined as a clinically significant AE (classified according to the NCI CTCAE version 5) or significant laboratory abnormality that occur during the DLT assessment periods, during dose escalation and dose expansion, and is considered by the Investigator to be related to GI-102.
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Study Day 1, assessed up to DLT period (3 weeks after treatment)

primaryOutcomes.measure: Incidence, nature, and severity of adverse events (AEs) and immune-related AEs (irAEs) (dose escalation phase of Part A and B)
primaryOutcomes.description: An adverse event (AE) is any untoward medical occurrence in a participant administered a pharmaceutical product and which does not necessarily have to have a causal relationship with the treatment. An AE can therefore be any unfavorable and unintended sign (including an abnormal laboratory finding, for example), symptom, or disease temporally associated with the use of a pharmaceutical product, whether or not considered related to the pharmaceutical product. Preexisting conditions which worsen during a study are also considered as AEs. All AE events will be graded according to National Cancer Institute (NCI) Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 5.0.
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Study Day 1, assessed up to approximately 24 months

primaryOutcomes.measure: Objective Response Rate (ORR) (dose optimization phase of Part A, dose expansion phase of Part B, Part C and D)
primaryOutcomes.description: ORR is defined as the percentage of participants with investigator-assessed objective response of complete response (CR) or partial response (PR). PR was defined as at least a 30% decrease in the sum of diameters of target lesions, taking as reference the baseline sum of diameters. CR was defined as disappearance of all target and non-target lesions and normalization of tumor marker levels (as applicable to non-target lesions).
primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Study Day 1, assessed up to approximately 24 months

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Objective Response Rate (ORR) (dose escalation phase of Part A and B)

An AE can therefore be any unfavorable and unintended sign (including an abnormal laboratory finding, for example), symptom, or disease temporally associated with the use of a pharmaceutical product, whether or not considered related to the pharmaceutical product. secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Study Day 1, assessed up to approximately 24 months

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Disease Control Rate (DCR)
secondaryOutcomes.description: DCR is defined as the percentage of patients who have achieved CR, PR and stable disease (SD), per RECIST v1.1 guideline as determined by the investigators.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Study Day 1, assessed up to approximately 24 months

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Duration of objective response (DoR)
secondaryOutcomes.description: DCR is defined as the time from the first occurrence of a documented objective response to the time of the first document disease progression or death from any cause, whichever occurs first, per RECIST v1.1 as determined by the investigator.
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: Study Day 1, assessed up to approximately 24 months

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Progression-free survival (PFS)
secondaryOutcomes.description: PFS is defined as the time from the first study treatment (Day 1) to the first occurrence of progression or death from any cause, whichever occurs first, per RECIST v1.1 guideline as determined by the investigator
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: 6-month, 12-month, and 18-month

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Overall survival (OS)
secondaryOutcomes.description: OS is defined as the time from the first study treatment to death from any cause
secondaryOutcomes.timeFrame: 12-month and 18-month
